steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package at the top of the file.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The file will have the necessary imports to use React and the useState hook.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the useFeatureFlag custom hook
steps.instruction: Create a custom hook function named useFeatureFlag that returns an array with two values: the current feature flag state and a toggle function.
steps.hint: Remember that custom hooks in React are just JavaScript functions that can call other hooks. Start with 'function useFeatureFlag()' or 'const useFeatureFlag = () =>'.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the useFeatureFlag custom hook here
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a useFeatureFlag function that will manage feature flag state and provide a way to toggle it.
successCriteria: A function named useFeatureFlag is defined and returns an array with two elements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the custom hook that will manage feature flag state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it's named exactly 'useFeatureFlag' and returns an array with two values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The custom hook wasn't created correctly. Check that you've defined a function named 'useFeatureFlag' that returns an array.

steps.title: Initialize feature flag state in the hook
steps.instruction: Inside the useFeatureFlag hook, call useState with an initial value of false to create the feature flag state.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported to create a state variable and its setter function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useFeatureFlag hook will have a state variable (e.g., isEnabled) initialized to false using useState.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called inside useFeatureFlag with false as the initial value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the feature flag state with useState.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling useState inside the useFeatureFlag hook with false as the initial value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires initializing state inside the useFeatureFlag hook. Try calling useState(false) within the hook function.

steps.title: Create toggle function in the hook
steps.instruction: Inside the useFeatureFlag hook, create a function named toggleFlag that updates the feature flag state to its opposite boolean value.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls the state setter function with the opposite of the current state value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useFeatureFlag hook now contains a toggleFlag function that can invert the boolean state value.
successCriteria: A toggleFlag function is defined inside useFeatureFlag that calls the state setter with the opposite boolean value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the toggleFlag function that will switch the feature flag state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure toggleFlag is defined as a function that calls the state setter with the opposite boolean value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggleFlag function isn't properly defined. It should be a function inside useFeatureFlag that toggles the boolean state.

steps.title: Return state and toggle from the hook
steps.instruction: Return an array containing the feature flag state and the toggle function from the useFeatureFlag hook.
steps.hint: At the end of your hook function, use a return statement with an array containing both values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useFeatureFlag hook now returns an array with the feature flag state and toggle function, making them available to components that use this hook.
successCriteria: The useFeatureFlag hook returns an array containing the state variable and toggle function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! Your hook now properly returns the state and toggle function, making them accessible to components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning an array with both the state variable and the toggle function from the hook.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hook should return an array containing both the feature flag state and the toggle function.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a function component called App that will contain the feature flag UI. The component should return null for now.
steps.hint: Define a function named App that returns null. This will be the main component that uses your custom hook.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have an App component function that returns null, ready to be filled with UI in later steps.
successCriteria: A function component named App is defined and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main App component. This will serve as the container for your feature flag UI.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've defined a function named App that returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component wasn't created correctly. Create a function named App that returns null.

steps.title: Use the feature flag hook in App
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, call the useFeatureFlag hook to get the feature flag state and toggle function.
steps.hint: Call the hook at the top of the component function to destructure its return values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have access to the feature flag state and toggle function.
successCriteria: The useFeatureFlag hook is called inside the App component, and its return values are destructured.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully called the custom hook inside your component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you call useFeatureFlag() and destructure its return values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hook call is missing or incorrect. Remember to call useFeatureFlag() at the top of the App component.

steps.title: Add conditional rendering based on feature flag
steps.instruction: In the App component's JSX, add a paragraph that conditionally renders based on the feature flag state. Use a ternary operator to show 'Feature is enabled!' when isEnabled is true, and 'Feature is disabled' when false.
steps.hint: You can use the isEnabled value from the hook in a ternary expression like: {isEnabled ? 'Feature is enabled!' : 'Feature is disabled'}
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will display different text based on whether the feature flag is enabled or disabled.
successCriteria: A paragraph element uses a ternary operator to conditionally render text based on the isEnabled value
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented conditional rendering based on the feature flag state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using a ternary operator with the isEnabled value to conditionally render the appropriate text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The conditional rendering isn't working as expected. Check that you're using the isEnabled value in a ternary expression within a paragraph element.

steps.title: Add toggle button and wire onClick
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside the App component's return statement that calls toggleFlag when clicked.
steps.hint: Add a <button> element with an onClick handler that references the toggleFlag function from the hook.
steps.expectedOutcome: A button element appears in the UI that toggles the feature flag when clicked.
successCriteria: The App component includes a button with an onClick handler that calls toggleFlag.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a button that will toggle the feature flag state when clicked.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but make sure its onClick handler correctly calls the toggleFlag function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button or its onClick handler is missing. Add a <button> with onClick={toggleFlag} inside the App component's return.

steps.title: Display feature flag status
steps.instruction: Update the paragraph inside the conditional rendering to show 'Feature is enabled' when the flag is on and 'Feature is disabled' when it's off.
steps.hint: Use the isEnabled state from the hook to determine which text to display. You can use a ternary operator or an if-else statement inside the paragraph.
steps.expectedOutcome: The paragraph will dynamically update to show 'Feature is enabled' or 'Feature is disabled' based on the current state of the feature flag.
successCriteria: The paragraph text changes correctly between 'Feature is enabled' and 'Feature is disabled' when the toggle button is clicked.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! The feature flag status is now clearly displayed in the UI, updating dynamically as you toggle the flag.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure the paragraph text changes between 'Feature is enabled' and 'Feature is disabled' based on the isEnabled state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph text doesn't seem to update correctly with the feature flag state. Check that you're using the isEnabled value to determine which text to display.
